content: I'll start by reading the test image and the part index file simultaneously.

The test image shows tomato leaves with:
- Extensive yellow/chlorotic patches on the leaf surface
- Small brownish spots scattered throughout

This is a **leaf** disease. Narrowing candidates from the leaf part index. Let me start viewing reference images one at a time.
Leaf_Mold shows yellow patches but lacks the numerous small dark spots visible in the test image. Let me check Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato next.
Bacterial_Speck shows small dark spots on largely green leaves - doesn't match the extensive yellowing in the test image. Let me check Septoria_Leaf_Blotch.
Septoria shows some yellowing with spots - partial match but let me continue exploring. Checking Target_Spot next.
Target_Spot doesn't match well - the reference shows spots on dark green leaves without the extensive yellowing. Checking Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus next.
TSWV doesn't match - shows ring spots and fruit symptoms. Checking Early_Blight next.
Early_Blight shows large dark spots with concentric rings - not matching the numerous small spots in the test image. Checking Verticillium_Wilt next.
Verticillium_Wilt shows V-shaped necrotic lesions and large yellowing - not matching. Checking Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus next.
CMV shows distorted, narrow leaves - not matching. Checking Powdery_Mildew next.
Powdery_Mildew shows white powdery patches - not matching. Checking Late_Blight next.
Late_Blight shows dark blotches and plant collapse - not matching. Checking Gray_Mold next.

Bacterial_Canker shows wilting with brown leaf margins - not matching. Checking Phytophthora_Blight next.
Phytophthora_Blight shows dark fruit rot and stem lesions - not matching. Checking Anthracnose next.
Anthracnose shows fruit rot - not matching. Checking Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers next.
Southern_Blight shows root/stem rot with white mycelium - not matching. Checking Bacterial_Wilt for my final view.

Now I've completed all 16 reference views. Let me analyze my findings.

**Summary of what I saw in the test image:**
- Tomato leaves with extensive yellow/chlorotic patches covering most of the leaf area
- Numerous small brownish spots scattered throughout the leaves
- Spots appear uniform in size and distribution
- Leaves still attached but significantly yellowed

**Comparison against reference images:**
- **Leaf_Mold**: Yellow patches on upper surface, but reference showed more diffuse mottling without many discrete dark spots
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Small spots on yellowing leaves - the top-right panel in the Septoria reference showed a yellowing leaf with scattered small spots, which most closely resembled the test image pattern
- All other candidates (Bacterial_Canker, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Powdery_Mildew, Anthracnose, etc.) showed clearly different symptoms (fruit rot, wilting, white powdery growth, distorted leaves)

**Decision:** The test image's pattern of numerous small discrete spots against extensive yellowing background best matches **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**. The KB describes small circular lesions with yellow halos that can overlap and merge, creating the widespread yellowing appearance seen in the test image. The Septoria reference images also showed yellowing leaves with scattered small spots most similar to the test image.
